texts.preamble: Raj Kumari And 39 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 27 January, 2020 Bench: Bala Krishna Narayana, Ravi Nath Tilhari High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 4 Case :- Writ - C No. - 1462 of 2020 Petitioner :- Raj Kumari And 39 Others Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Petitioner :- Radhey Shyam Dwivedi
texts.facts: This writ petition has been filed by the petitioners with the following prayers : "(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to protect the petitioners from eviction by the respondents from their site of squatting/vending as per the mandate of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 as well as notification dated 15.06.2017 of the Chief Secretary for implementation of Section 3(3) of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014. Raj Kumari And 39 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 27 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168793707/ 1 (ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents not to dispossess or evict or disturb the petitioners from their site of vending at Sector-2 & 14 Noida Gautam Buddha Nagar U.P. till the certificate or license is granted to the petitioners as per Section 3 of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014. (iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to protect the petitioners till the respondents frames the rules, schemes etc. alongwith the constitution of TVC and demarcation of vending and non vending zone and grant of license as per the eligibility and merits for their interrupted and peaceful vending. (v) Award the cost of the writ petition in favour of the petitioners." This writ petition has been filed by ten petitioners seeking following prayers : "(a) Protect the petitioners from eviction by the respondents from their site of squatting/vending as per the mandate of The Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 as per the order of this Hon'ble High Court dated 31.05.2017 passed in Writ-C No.17013 of 2017 titled "Dr. Bheem Rao Ambedkar K. P. Dainik Vyapari Welfare Association Vs. State of U. P. and others" as well as Notification/Shashanadesh for implementation of Section 3 (3) of The Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 and also the order passed in the matter of "Rekha Singh vs. State of U. p. and others" vide PIL No.26422 of 2017 dated 16.06.2017. (b) [LEAKAGE_MASK] the Press Release dated 25.07.2019 of respondent no.2, which is against the mandate of the provisions of the act and the Rules thereunder along with the Government orders mentioned (supra) and the orders passed by this Hon'ble High Court mentioned (supra) along with several other orders passed since 2014. (c) Direct the respondents not to dispossess or evict or disturb the petitioners from their site of vending at Sector-58-59, Noida, Gautam Budh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh till the certificate or license is granted to the petitioners as per Section 3 of The Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014. (d) Protect the petitioners till the respondents frames the Rules, Schemes etc. along with the Constitution of TVC and demarcation of vending and non-vending zone and grant of license as per the eligibility and merits for their uninterrupted and peaceful vending and squatting to earn their livelihood at their site." 3. Case set up by petitioners is that fundamental rights guaranteed to petitioners under Article 14 and 19 (1) (g) of the Constitution for doing business is being violated by respondent authorities by removing street vending shops from their respective sites at Sector 58-59 of Noida and not allowing them to continue their business. They are being harassed by authorities/ respondents abrupting their livelihood and some times they are not allowed to squat and vend at their site. Petitioners' business is in no way hindrance to either smooth pedestrian movements or obstruction to pavement or parking. Petitioners are dealing in night markets in the area where Call centres of various MNCs, Media Houses and various other business centres which are operating at night catering to the international market and country, providing the call centres, business centres and items related thereto to all the employees at night, without any disturbance to any public and pedestrian movement as well as vehicular movement. Petitioners i.e vendors and squatters in order to have legally vending business have complied with various Rules and Regulations in terms of Food Licenses for Food Safety and Health Standards as mandated by Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as "FSSAI"), Section 26-C of Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 1973") and carrying on their business without any encroachment. Photographs of sites are also placed on record. It is said that protecting rights of street vendors, various orders have been passed from time to time but ignoring all these orders and also provisions under "The Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014" (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 2014") and rules framed thereunder i.e. "The Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Rules, 2017 (hereinafter referred to as "Rules, 2017") " respondent 3 has issued a press release for removal of petitioners' street vending stalls/shops etc., which is patently illegal.
texts.arguments: (iv) Issue any other writ, order or direction, which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the issue involved in this writ petition was subject matter of another writ petition namely Writ C No. 28417 of 2019 which was finally disposed of by another co-ordinate Bench of this Court by order dated 17.09.2019 and hence this writ petition may also be disposed of on the same terms and conditions subject to which the aforesaid writ petition was decided. Learned standing counsel does not dispute the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioners. The judgment and order dated 17.09.2019 passed by another co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Writ C No. 28417 of 2019 is being reproduced hereinbelow : "1. Heard Sri Michael Peter, learned counsel for petitioners, learned Standing Counsel for respondents 1, 3 and 4 and Sri Kaushlendra Nath Singh, learned counsel for respondent 2. 2. 4. Learned counsel for petitioners placed before us various orders of this Court as well as Act, 2014 and in particular Section 3 of Act, 2014 which provides for survey of street vendors and protection from eviction or relocation till completion of Survey and allotment of alternative site. He contended that unless a survey of street vendors is conducted by Town Vending Committee, petitioners cannot be removed. Learned counsel appearing for respondent 2 submitted that petitioners have encroached upon public land causing obstruction in free flow of traffic and, therefore, authorities have issued notices to petitioners directing them to vacate the site or they shall be removed. 6. Section 3 of Act, 2014 reads as under :- "3. Survey of street vendors and protection from eviction or relocation.-(1) The Town Vending Committee shall, within such period and in such manner as may be specified in the scheme, conduct a survey of all existing street vendors, within the area under its jurisdiction, and subsequent survey shall be carried out at least once in every five years. (2) The Town Vending Committee shall ensure that all existing street vendors, identified in the survey, are accommodated in the vending zones subject to a norm conforming to two and half per cent of the population of the ward or zone or town or city, as the case may be, in accordance with the plan for street vending and the holding capacity of the vending zones. (3) No street vendor shall be evicted or, as the case may be, relocated till the survey specified under sub-section (1) has been completed and the certificate of vending is issued to all street vendors." 8. Section 4 of Act, 2014 provides for issue of certificate of vending and reads as under :- "4. Issue of certificate of vending.-(1) Every street vendor, identified under the survey carried out under sub-section (1) of Section 3, who has completed the age of fourteen years or such age as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government, shall be issued a certificate of vending by the Town Vending Committee, subject to such terms and conditions and within the period specified in the scheme including the restrictions specified in the plan for street vending: Provided that a person, whether or not included under the survey under sub-section (1) of Section 3, who has been issued a certificate of vending before the Raj Kumari And 39 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 27 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168793707/ 4 commencement of this Act, whether known as licence or any other form of permission (whether as a stationary vendor or a mobile vendor or under any other category) shall be deemed to be a street vendor for that category for the period for which he has been issued such certificate of vending. ( 2) Where, in the intervening period between two surveys, any person seeks to vend, the Town Vending Committee may grant a certificate of vending to such person, subject to the scheme, the plan for street vending and the holding capacity of the vending zones. (3) Where the number of street vendors identified under sub-section (1) or the number of persons seeking to vend under sub-section (2) are more than the holding capacity of the vending zone and exceeds the number of persons to be accommodated in that vending zone, the Town Vending Committee shall carry out a draw of lots for issuing the certificate of vending for that vending zone and the remaining persons shall be accommodated in any adjoining vending zone to avoid relocation." 9. Section 14 of Act, 2014 provides duty of street vendors and reads as under :- "14. Duty of street vendors.-Where a street vendor occupies space on a time sharing basis, he shall remove his goods and wares every day at the end of the time sharing period allowed to him." 10. Sections 15 and 16 of Act, 2014 deal with maintenance of cleanliness and public hygiene and maintenance of civic amenities in vending zone in good condition respectively and read as under :- "15. Maintenance of cleanliness and public hygiene.-Every street vendor shall maintain cleanliness and public hygiene in the vending zones and the adjoining areas." "16. Maintenance of civic amenities in vending zone in good condition.-Every street vendor shall maintain civic amenities and public property in the vending zone in good condition and not damage or destroy or cause any damage or destruction to the same." 11. Supreme Court has also considered rights of 'Street Vendor' and in Maharashtra Ekta Hawkers Union and Ors. Vs. Municipal Corporation, Greater Mumbai and Ors. , 2004 (1) SCC 625 has said as under :- "The above authorities made it clear that the hawkers have a right under Article 19 (1) (g) of the Constitution of India. Thus, hawking may not be permitted where e.g. due to narrowness of road, free flow of traffic or movement of pedestrians is hindered or where for security reasons an area is required to be kept free or near Hospitals, places Raj Kumari And 39 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 27 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168793707/ 5 of worship etc. 13. Learned counsel for petitioners submitted that in para 15 of this petition, he has stated that petitioners are making no encroachment or obstruction in smooth running of commuters/metro riders. 14. However, we find that this is a disputed question of fact, since, respondents are proceeding to remove petitioners from the sites on the ground that they have encroached upon the same causing hindrance to smooth pedestrian movements or obstructions to pavement or parking.
